title: Retirement is 100% scope-id-keyed — semantically identical work re-derived under a fresh id (retro-<cycle>-<slug>-<fp> autofiles, P0 prescriptions, eval-born slugs) sails past every guard
summary: Alignment-audit finding (ADR-0089 gap #3, confirmed in code): auto-filed ids embed the cycle number (failure_learning.go:501-534) so a later cycle's identical defect mints a new id; dedup checks exact paths/ids only (faillearn/inbox.go writeIfAbsent; retrofile existingIDs). Live instance: cycle-1505's lane re-derived the parked retirement scope from a stale P0's prescription. ADR-0089 never claimed this scope — genuine open gap, the FOURTH re-dispatch channel (semantic, not typed).
root_cause: Identity = id string; no content/semantic linkage across cycles or between prescriptions and existing (incl. parked/consumed) items.
fix: DESIGN-leaning: (a) cheap first slice — autofiled/P0-prescribed items carry a normalized content fingerprint (title+files slug-set hash); filers check it against pending+parked+recently-consumed before minting (log+skip on match); (b) triage guidance: prescriptions naming a parked scope defer to the parked item rather than minting. Avoid over-engineering semantic similarity — exact normalized-fingerprint match only.
acceptance: Autofiler skips (loudly) when the normalized fingerprint matches an existing pending/parked/consumed-recent item — red-first with the cycle-1505 shape.
No suppression of genuinely-new defects (distinct fingerprints mint as today).
connects_to: ADR-0089 (explicitly out of its stated scope)
notes: Filed from the alignment audit; scoped deliberately to exact-fingerprint matching.
